architect.cite: a driver whose probe passes is seated in rotation with no decision
architect.reply_head:
Yes

The amendment is small and you can check it against the record. It touches one entry, adds 3 lines to the agreement, and the 60-minute probe window can be confirmed from the committed probe file's timestamp against the declaration commit. Making the "probe passes, so seat it with no decision" step automatic removes stale-belief judgment calls, and that is the failure the evidence shows. One amendment line per seat change is easy to audit with git.

Notes, not conditions:
- Define the exit from Probation (one passing smoke plus one clean seat) so it can't drag on.
- Spell out that a quota or balance failure is not a behaviour finding. Oth

developer.cite: a misbehaving driver is repaired, not benched
developer.reply_head:
Yes

From the developer's seat, the rules are workable and I can follow them honestly. A probe within 60 minutes is cheap. Seating a driver whose probe passes with no decision takes away guesswork. A repaired driver has to pass a smoke test in a throwaway worktree before it gets a Probation seat, which protects the red-then-green order instead of weakening it.

audit lens.cite: every seat plan and Decider window cites a probe_all.py output taken within 60 minutes
audit lens.reply_head:
No
The proposal mandates committing probe outputs and amendment lines, but leaves a verifiability loophole: committing a file proves nothing about live execution or data freshness, and repairs in a throwaway worktree leave zero git trace. The team could commit static or stale artifacts and claim compliance, passing the vote while breaking the practice. Git alone cannot verify behavioral fixes or live probe validity without structural constraints.
Require the probe output to include a verifiable system-state hash and mandate that all repair smoke tests be committed to a tracked worktree, with a machine-readable schema validated by the gate rev

coach.cite: Seat plans follow a live probe
coach.reply_head:
Yes
Right-sized as an Experimental entry: one owner, 3-card trial, hypothesis with metric, counter-metric, and target 0. It adds only lightweight checks — a 60-minute probe, one amendment line per seat change, and a retro list — proportionate to the benched capacity and two undeclared swaps evidenced. No new seats or standing ceremony.

architect.cite: a hash of machine state is not something git can verify
architect.reply_head:
Yes

The amendment strengthens the design without adding scope. A fixed schema, a 60-minute freshness rule and a committed repair record are all things git can check. Rejecting the machine-state hash is correct because git cannot verify it. The "without a recorded cause" escape keeps the check from flagging a seat the rotation rule correctly refused. One note: the check should read the cause from a named field of the seat plan, not from free text, so that the planted-fail tests can be checked by a machine.

qa.cite: the check and its planted-fail tests are written red first as a tooling card filed with this pick
qa.reply_head:
I'll read the amendment, the patch, and the original QA condition without changing anything, then vote only on whether that condition is met.I'll compare the original QA condition to the regenerated patch and the live probe schema.Yes

The form names `check_seat_plan.py`, planted-fail tests written red first as a tooling card, and a non-zero exit when the plan omits a driver whose cited probe passed. That is the check I required. Hand-running the same three checks until the card lands keeps the rule testable in the trial. Condition met; I support the proposal.

developer.cite: a repair is committed as `driver-repairs.md` under the card
developer.reply_head:
Yes

The amendment doesn't change my vote. From the developer's seat, `check_seat_plan.py` gives three exact exit conditions: a missing schema field, a probe row older than 60 minutes, or an available driver left out of the plan with no recorded cause. Its planted-fail tests are written red first as their own tooling card, so I can do that work without gaming it. Note: the closure check should refuse a card when a driver it sidelined has no `driver-repairs.md`.

audit lens.cite: a hash of machine state is not something git can verify
audit lens.reply_head:
No
The verifiable system-state hash is not met, as the proposal explicitly notes it cannot be verified by git.

decider.cite: seats benched while the driver was available or fixable
decider.reply_head:
Yes
The evaluation is framed so that deciding to adopt, reshape, or reject rests on objective evidence: explicit targets for benched seats and undeclared swaps against repair minutes across a 3-card trial. With the amendment, probe freshness and schema compliance are verified by `check_seat_plan.py`, and driver repairs leave a committed git trace in `driver-repairs.md` with smoke test outputs. The team has every seat required to verify and sign off.

coach.cite: Seat plans follow a live probe
coach.reply_head:
Yes
Amendment adds no seat or ceremony layer. It automates the probe, freshness, and omission checks, with manual checks only until that tooling lands. That is proportionate to the stale-benching problem.

audit lens.cite: The hash binds a row to a commit and makes an edited row detectable
audit lens.reply_head:
Yes

The condition is met in the form git can check. Each probe row carries the commit it was taken against and a hash that `check_seat_plan.py` recomputes. Repair smoke tests are committed under the card, and the same script checks their schema. One caveat, not a new demand: the hash has no secret, so it shows an edit only if the hash wasn't recomputed. The entry already says the hash doesn't prove the probe ran live.

audit lens.cite: the hash binds a row to a commit and makes an edited row detectable
audit lens.reply_head:
Yes.
The second amendment replaces the unverifiable system-state hash with a row_sha256 bound to the repository head commit, which git can verify to detect edits. Repair smoke tests are now committed in driver-repairs.md with schema validation handled by check_seat_plan.py, satisfying the verifiability and traceability requirements within git's constraints.
